title: Overland AI unveils autonomous Ibex vehicle
source_used: Automotive World (its text matches Overland AI's launch statement, also carried by ASDNews); the Axios exclusive (feed source) returned a block
key_facts: Overland AI has launched Ibex, a fully autonomous ground vehicle for the US military, built on the Polaris MRZR's chassis, engine and drivetrain.
Ibex carries a 2,000-pound payload, drives over 35 mph in full autonomy, and has a 250-mile range at 20 mph on one tank of diesel or JP-8.
The US Marine Corps has chosen Ibex for integration into its counter-drone system, the Marine Air Defense Integrated System.
Overland AI says Ibex needs no remote control or teleoperation and that it is the first ground autonomy company to prime a production contract for the US military.
Greg Okopal, co-founder and chief operating officer of Overland AI, says Ibex can be deployed on day one with parts and fuel the units already use.
quote_evidence: Overland AI has launched Ibex, a fully autonomous ground vehicle for the US military built on the in-service Polaris MRZR’s chassis, engine and drivetrain.
It needs no remote control or teleoperation, relying on Overland AI’s OverDrive software to cross difficult terrain with degraded communications.
why_it_matters_hint: A self-driving vehicle moves into US Marine Corps counter-drone work.
notes: Axios exclusive (feed source) blocked by Cloudflare. ASDNews (asdnews.com, 7 Oct) carries the same company release. The first-contract claim and the performance figures are the company's.
